source.value: Consider the curve  $\mathbf r(t)=\left\langle 2t-1 ,\: 8t+2 ,\: -2t \right\rangle, \, t \geq 0,$ for which the arc length $s$ from $\mathbf{r}(0)$ to $\mathbf{r}(t)$ is given by $s=6\sqrt{2}t.$ Find $\mathbf R(s),$ the parametrization of the curve by its arc length $s.$

decisions.reason: Observed MA content supersedes the stored value

decisions.question: e-3065

source.question: e-3065
source.value:
First, since  $s=6\sqrt{2}t,$ we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}6\sqrt{2}t & =s \\ t & =\frac{s}{6\sqrt{2}} \\ t & =\frac{\sqrt{2}s}{12}.\end{aligned}
$$

The vector function that pametrizes the curve $\mathbf r(t)$ by its arc length $s,$ with $s \geq 0,$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}R(s) & =r(\frac{\sqrt{2}s}{12}) \\  & =⟨2(\frac{\sqrt{2}s}{12})-1,\,8(\frac{\sqrt{2}s}{12})+2,\,-2(\frac{\sqrt{2}s}{12})⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\sqrt{2}s}{6}-1,\,\frac{4\sqrt{2}s}{6}+2,\,-\frac{\sqrt{2}s}{6}⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{6}⟨\sqrt{2}s-6,\,4\sqrt{2}s+12,\,-\sqrt{2}s⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

source.value: Given the curve  $\mathbf r(t)=\cos{t}\,\mathbf i - \sin{t}\,\mathbf j+\sqrt{3}t\,\mathbf k, \, t \geq 0,$ for which the arc length $s$ from $\mathbf r(0)$ to $\mathbf r(t)$ is given by $s=2t,$ find the corresponding unit tangent $\mathbf{T}(s),$ parametrized by $s.$

decisions.reason: Observed MA content supersedes the stored value

decisions.question: e-3067

source.question: e-3067
source.value:
First, since $s=2t,$ we have that $t=\dfrac{s}{2}.$

Therefore, the vector function $\mathbf R(s)$ that parametrizes $\mathbf r(t)$ by its arc length is

$$
\begin{aligned}R(s) & =r(\frac{s}{2}) \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{2})\,i-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{2})\,j+\sqrt{3}\cdot \frac{s}{2}k \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{2})\,i-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{2})\,j+\frac{\sqrt{3}s}{2}\,k.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Now, since the curve is parametrized by its arc length $s,$ the unit tangent can be found as

$$
\mathbf T(s) = \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}s}\mathbf R(s).
$$

So, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}T(s) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}R(s) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{2}))\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{2}))j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\frac{\sqrt{3}s}{2})k \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{2})\,i-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{2})\,j+\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\,k \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{2})\,i-\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{2})\,j+\sqrt{3}\,k).\end{aligned}
$$

decisions.question: e-3066

source.question: e-3066
source.value: What is the parametrization of the curve  $\mathbf r(t)=2(t\cos{t}-\sin{t})\,\mathbf i+2(t\sin{t}+\cos{t})\,\mathbf j, \, t \geq 0$ by its arc length $s?$

decisions.reason: Observed MA content supersedes the stored value

decisions.question: e-3066

source.question: e-3066
source.value:
First, we find $\mathbf{r}'(t)$ and its magnitude $\|\mathbf{r}'(t)\|\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =2\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t\operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\,i+2\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t\operatorname{sin}⁡t+\operatorname{cos}⁡t)\,j \\  & =2(\operatorname{cos}⁡t-t\operatorname{sin}⁡t-\operatorname{cos}⁡t)\,i+2(\operatorname{sin}⁡t+t\operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\,j \\  & =-2t\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i+2t\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j \\ ‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =|2t|\sqrt{(-\operatorname{sin}⁡t)^{2}+{cos}^{2}⁡t} \\  & =2t\end{aligned}
$$

Note that in the last step, we removed the absolute value bars since $t>0.$ 

Next, we calculate the arc length of the curve from $0$ to $t\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}s & ={\int }_{0}^{t}‖{r}^{′}(u)‖\,\text{d}u \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{t}2u\,\text{d}u \\  & ={u}^{2}{|}_{0}^{t} \\  & ={t}^{2}-0 \\  & ={t}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since $s=t^2,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{t}^{2} & =s \\ t & =\pm \sqrt{s} \\ t & =\sqrt{s},\end{aligned}
$$

taking the positive root because $t>0.$  

Finally, the vector function that parametrizes $\mathbf r(t)$ by its arc length is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}R(s) & =r(\sqrt{s}) \\  & =2(\sqrt{s}\operatorname{cos}⁡\sqrt{s}-\operatorname{sin}⁡\sqrt{s})\,i+2(\sqrt{s}\operatorname{sin}⁡\sqrt{s}+\operatorname{cos}⁡\sqrt{s})\,j.\end{aligned}
$$
